business-website.subheadline: From a one-page landing to a full 5-10 page site: custom design, mobile-first, built to turn visitors into calls, appointments and form submissions.
business-website.content: Your website is often the first contact a customer has with your business, and it works while you are busy with everything else. I build business websites that load in under two seconds, read well on a phone and make it obvious how to call you or book. Every site is designed mobile-first because most people looking for a local service are searching from their phones. I use Next.js and React, the same stack large companies rely on, so the site stays fast and keeps ranking as it grows. A landing page has a fixed price and can be started right here; a larger site is quoted after a short conversation about the pages you need. English and Spanish versions are included when your customers speak both, written by a native Spanish speaker rather than a translator plugin.

website-redesign.headline: Website Redesign & Modernization
website-redesign.subheadline: Your current site rebuilt on modern technology: faster, mobile-friendly and easier for customers to use, with your content and your Google rankings carried over.
website-redesign.content: An old website costs you customers quietly: it loads slowly on phones, looks dated next to competitors and is hard to update. A redesign is not just a new coat of paint. I rebuild the site on Next.js, keep every page and URL that already ranks, set up redirects for anything that moves and migrate your content, photos and reviews. The result is a site that loads in under two seconds, works on every screen and that you can keep updating without breaking it. That is what I did for GSM A/C, whose rebuilt site went from a slow template to a fast, conversion-focused site that now books jobs on its own. The price depends on how many pages you have and what needs to be rewritten, so we agree on the scope first.

admin-dashboard.content: Most small businesses run on a mix of spreadsheets, text messages and three different apps that do not talk to each other. A custom admin dashboard puts that in one place: your leads come in from the website, you see who called, who paid and who needs a follow-up, and campaigns go out by email or SMS from the same screen. I build these panels with Next.js, TypeScript and PostgreSQL, the stack this very site runs on, and connect them to the tools you already use, such as Stripe, Google or Twilio. The scope is tailored to how you work: for GSM A/C the dashboard replaced about fifteen hours a week of manual follow-up. We start with a conversation about your daily routine, agree on what the first version needs to do, and build from there.

store-and-apps.subheadline: Full-featured online stores with Stripe and custom platforms built around your business: booking systems, member areas, internal tools. No monthly platform fees.
store-and-apps.content: Template platforms are a quick start and a long-term ceiling: monthly fees, limited customization, slow pages and plugins that break on every update. When your business outgrows them, I build the store or the platform you actually need. An online store includes Stripe payment processing, real-time inventory, order tracking, customer accounts and an admin panel where you run everything. A custom web application can be a booking system like the one RC Beauty Salon uses, a member area, a portal for your clients or an internal tool for your team. You own the code, pay only for hosting and Stripe's standard fees, and every feature is built for your workflow. Projects this size start with a scoping conversation and a written quote, then a 50% deposit to begin.

maintenance.headline: Monthly Maintenance & Support
maintenance.subheadline: Ongoing maintenance, security updates, backups and technical support so your website keeps working while you run your business.
maintenance.content: A website is not finished when it launches. Dependencies get security updates, hosting and domains renew, content goes stale and one day a form stops sending. The maintenance plan covers that for any site I built: I keep the stack updated, monitor uptime and performance, keep backups, make the small content changes you send me and answer technical questions the same day when something is urgent. It is a monthly subscription paid through Stripe that you can cancel at any time from the link in your invoice email. If you need bigger changes, such as a new page or a new feature, I quote them separately so the monthly price stays predictable.
